rationale: Suspicious: 3 signal(s) needing review; e.g. network request to a runtime-assembled url.

findings.title: Network request to a runtime-assembled URL
findings.detail: new WebSocket() targets a runtime-assembled URL containing the external fragment wss://ws.brewser.io/?app=.

findings.title: Declares `network` with an empty allowed_origins allowlist
findings.detail: The manifest declares the full `network` permission but lists no allowed_origins, so the runtime applies no per-origin restriction to its fetch/XHR/WebSocket traffic. Note media and image element loads are exempt from the allowlist anyway, so streaming from un-enumerable CDN hosts is not a reason to leave it empty. Confirm the fetch destinations cannot be enumerated; if they can, declare them.

findings.title: Realtime-relay app id is assembled at runtime
findings.detail: Builds a Brewser realtime-relay URL at runtime without pinning the app id to "com.natureglass.artistemultiplayerpaint". Confirm it cannot resolve to another package's namespace.

limitations: Static heuristic scan. A GOOD verdict means no known-bad pattern matched, NOT proof of safety. Human review is still required for every submission.
